Purpose: Sets the overarching framework, objectives and responsibilities for the company's information security activities.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Security lead
Sections and tables: Scope and systems in scope (table: Software | Purpose) · Security objectives (table: Objective | Measurement) · Requirements and interested parties (table, from the Requirement lines below) · Communication plan (ISO 27001 only) · Control oversight (platform or register) · Statement of Applicability (ISO 27001) · Supporting policies · Continual improvement
Options and asks:
Options: objectives menu, pick three to six that fit Compliance Goals · ESG reporting.
Ask for: scope exclusions, if any · the measure behind each objective · communication plan rows (ISO 27001)
Build notes: Build it last, so the supporting-policy list and the systems table match what was built. Say 'ISMS' only when ISO/IEC 27001 is in scope. The systems table lists only tools the brain names, one line each; the Access Control Policy uses the same table, so keep them identical. The requirements table takes only requirements the brain names. Every objective needs a measure the client can report. A Responsible Disclosure Policy isn't in this library: list one only if the client has it.

Purpose: Sets the behaviour expected of everyone: representing the company's values and building trust, giving customers, partners and stakeholders a good experience, and supporting company objectives through performance and culture.
Owners:
Accountable: Governance Lead
Responsible: People lead
Sections and tables: Company values (the client's own text) · Required behaviours: conduct, confidentiality and policies, performance appraisals · Elective conduct · Environmental conduct · Breaches: reporting and discipline
Options and asks:
Options: elective conduct (leave, expenses, grooming, housekeeping, social media, wellness) for larger teams · environmental conduct when the client reports on ESG.
Ask for: company values or mission statement · where the disciplinary process is documented
Build notes: Keep it short and in the client's voice. Paste the client's own values; never write values for them, and leave the section out if there are none. Founders and owners generally don't need appraisals (AI Guidance 4.1). Control GV-04 expects the disciplinary process to be stated: point to the HR procedure if one exists. Elective and environmental items only on request.

Purpose: Sets how everyone supports the security of the company's systems and data: managing devices, handling sensitive information, protecting credentials and behaving in security-aware ways.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Security lead
Sections and tables: General security behaviours: agreements and confidentiality, data minimisation, awareness and reporting, paper, screens and unattended devices · Systems and devices: approved storage and business use, device baseline, password manager, software and cloud services · Network security: networks and travel · Authentication and passwords · Data handling, with one line per regulated-data law · Devices: company devices, personal devices (BYOD)
Options and asks:
Options: stricter device rules (device firewall on, biometric unlock, no customer data on devices), only where enforced · VPN wording where one is used.
Ask for: screen-lock time enforced · where the approved software and cloud services list lives · whether a VPN is used
Build notes: The policy staff acknowledge most often, so every line must be something they can do. Device rules must match what device management enforces, including the screen-lock minutes. For a fully remote team this policy carries the physical security rules; with offices they sit in the Physical Security Policy and the screen rule is headed with the locations. Regulated data: one line per law in Regulatory Drivers, from the Requirement lines below. Endpoint model BYOD or Mixed: control EP-05 adds company data only through managed apps or browser sessions, and no personal devices in production. Corporate managed: say personal devices aren't used for work, once confirmed.

Built from: POL-05 · POL-05.01–05.15 (05.06 moves to the Password Policy when that is built separately)
Purpose: Defines the logical access control requirements that protect the company's systems and data from unauthorised access.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Security lead
Sections and tables: Scope and systems (the same table as the Information Security Policy) · Access rules: access to ePHI (HIPAA), least privilege, identity and authentication, password manager · Access lifecycle: approval, removal, review · Privileged access: mechanism by shape, segregation of duties · Permitted use · Authentication secrets and connections · Policy compliance
Options and asks:
Options: password manager travel mode, if the tool has it and the client uses it.
Ask for: where access approvals and removals are recorded · any shared or break-glass accounts
Build notes: Word approval, review and privileged access to fit the shapes. Access ownership sets the approver: a central team with manager or system-owner approval, or the system owner; in a small team the person granting access may also approve it. Privileged & production access sets the mechanism: standing (list reviewed quarterly), temporary (approved per need, then removed) or just in time (approval workflow, automatic expiry). Founders and owners may hold admin access and deploy by role (AI Guidance 4.1): write segregation of duties for the wider team. Removal time and review frequency can't be weaker than controls AC-02 and AC-03. Shared and service accounts need a named owner (AC-11). Usually prints the policy compliance clause.

Built from: POL-05.06 and POL-02.03 · a supporting part of the Access Control Policy
Purpose: The use of secure, strong passwords to protect the company's systems and data from unauthorised access.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Security lead
Sections and tables: Minimum password requirements (list of the six settings: minimum length, maximum age, reuse history, complexity, lockout threshold, lockout duration) · Password manager · User responsibilities
Options and asks: Ask for: the password settings the identity provider and key systems enforce
Build notes: Print only settings the systems enforce; don't print a rotation or complexity rule the systems don't apply (see Settings to confirm). Keep the user rules identical to the Acceptable Use Policy and the password-manager wording identical to the Access Control Policy. Light depth: a section of the Access Control Policy rather than a separate document.

Built from: POL-09 · POL-09.01–09.07, with POL-08.03 for production databases
Purpose: Defines roles, responsibilities and requirements for managing the company's information assets (people, devices, documented information, databases, source code repositories and software) so they stay secure, available and accurate.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Security lead
Sections and tables: Asset records (employee list, device register, key-document portal and register, source code repositories, architecture diagram, central logs) · People · Devices: device management (tool or register), asset disposal · Documents: key documents · Databases: production databases · Source code · Software · Policy compliance
Options and asks: Ask for: where the device register and key-document register are kept · how devices are wiped and disposed of
Build notes: List only the records the client keeps, and name the tool that holds each (HR system, device management, knowledge base, code repository, logging); drop any record they don't keep. With no device management tool, control EP-01 checks device settings at least quarterly, so say so. Production databases: encryption at rest, restricted direct access, regular backups and a restore test, with the frequency from the Backup Policy. Usually prints the policy compliance clause.

Document: Data Classification, Handling and Retention Policy
Purpose: Sets how data is managed to meet security, availability and integrity objectives, with protection and retention that vary by sensitivity, risk and compliance requirements.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Security lead
Sections and tables: Classification levels: Restricted, Confidential, Internal, Public; personal data as Private; regulated classes (CDR data, ePHI) for laws in scope · Handling: collection, protection and storage, labelling, approvals and backup · Retention and disposal: retention periods, archiving and disposal · Data register (table: Data type | Classification | Responsible owner | Retention period | Requirements)
Options and asks:
Options: no sensitive data on end-user devices (stricter; keep in step with the Acceptable Use Policy) · document naming protocol.
Ask for: retention period for each record type · data register rows · naming protocol, if any
Build notes: Keep the four levels and fit the examples to Data Handled; 'sensitive' means all non-public data. Retention must agree with contracts, the privacy policy and local law, so confirm every period (starting table under Settings to confirm). Regulated classes only for laws in Regulatory Drivers. The data register starts from Data Handled and Data Collected on the System Description tab; the client confirms each row. Name the privacy laws that apply to personal data.

Purpose: Keeps information and communications secure across the company's networks and systems: wired and wireless, public and internal networks, remote connections, and monitoring that detects suspicious activity and vulnerabilities.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Security lead
Sections and tables: Firewalls (deny by default, restricted administration, configuration review) · Web application firewall · Firewall change alerts · Logging and alerting · Monitoring tool · Threat detection · Encryption · Hardening baseline · Serverless architecture · Compliance monitoring · Policy compliance
Options and asks:
Options: firewall change alerts, only if the alert exists · hardening baseline (a control from Scaleup stage, or when a cloud configuration tool is named).
Ask for: which statements are configured today (firewall rules, alerts, hardening baseline)
Build notes: Every line is a claim an auditor can test against configuration, so state only what is switched on. Word firewalls for the real architecture: security groups or the provider's equivalent in cloud; managed endpoints with restricted resource policies for serverless (NS-01). Controls LM-01 and LM-02: logs kept at least one year, alerts to responsible personnel. Name the monitoring tool from Availability Monitoring, or Audit Logging if that is where events are logged. Usually prints the policy compliance clause.

Built from: POL-08.02–08.04 · supports the Network Security Policy
Purpose: Defines responsibilities and requirements for the cryptographic controls that protect the privacy, confidentiality and integrity of sensitive data.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Security lead
Sections and tables: Encryption scope (table: System | Type | Algorithm, covering infrastructure and the website in transit, production data stores at rest, staff laptops, and a VPN if used) · Key management · Key management service · Sub-processors
Options and asks: Ask for: encryption settings for data in transit and at rest · key rotation practice
Build notes: Check the real settings before naming an algorithm; one table row per real system. Control NS-05 rotates keys at least annually. If customers hold their own keys (Data control boundary), say so. Light depth: a section of the Data Management Policy.

Built from: POL-09.08–09.10 · only when Facilities isn't None – fully remote (or is unanswered)
Purpose: Protects the company's information assets from unauthorised physical access. Supported by the Asset Management Policy and Acceptable Use Policy.
Owners:
Accountable: Governance Lead
Responsible: Security lead
Sections and tables: Locations (each site: type of premises and what is kept there) · Employee responsibilities: secure behaviour, entry and visitors · Office premises: premises controls · Access review and removal
Options and asks:
Options: premises controls, stating only what each building has (electronic identification, access passes, individually assigned access, visitor sign-in, monitored reception, CCTV, contracted security).
Ask for: office locations · the physical controls each site has, and who runs them
Build notes: Only for clients with premises. Facilities gives the type of site, not where it is, so ask for locations. Many controls belong to the landlord or co-working provider: say who runs them. Production hosting is covered by the cloud provider's assurance report (VM-05), not this policy. Control PS-01 reviews physical access at least annually and removes it at off-boarding.

Built from: POL-06 · POL-06.01–06.06 · usually one document with the Controls Assessment Program
Purpose: Defines how the company identifies, assesses, treats, monitors and reports the risks to its objectives, and the controls that mitigate them.
Owners:
Accountable: Governance Lead
Responsible: Compliance Owner
Sections and tables: Risk cycle (identify, assess, treat, monitor, report; review cadence; reporting to the board) · Risk areas, including fraud and a line per law in scope · Register and assessment · Rating criteria (3×3 grid) · Treatment (threshold, owners, residual acceptance) · Monitoring and reporting
Options and asks:
Options: ESG wording ('our impact on the environment and society') when the client reports on ESG.
Ask for: whether there is a board · dollar bands for impact · who attends risk reviews
Build notes: Fit reviews to the Operating Cadence instead of adding meetings. Fraud must be considered (RM-01). Follow the Risk management shape: Periodic is a scheduled assessment; Continuous updates the register as changes, incidents and vendor reviews occur, with a full review at least annually (RM-02). The rating grid, bands and appetite come from the Risks tab: don't invent a second scale. Board: ask whether there is one; if not, name who oversees leadership, such as the founders. Board oversight is a control only at Enterprise stage (GV-08).

Built from: POL-01.08, 01.10 and POL-06 · usually in the same document as the Risk Management Framework
Purpose: Defines roles, responsibilities and requirements for an effective internal control framework: controls that mitigate the risks in the Risk Management Framework and meet compliance requirements, kept appropriate, effective, documented and improving.
Owners:
Accountable: Governance Lead
Responsible: Compliance Owner
Sections and tables: Control framework (platform or register) · Control self-assessments · External audit · Internal audit (ISO 27001, or Enterprise stage) · Competency and corrective actions (ISO 27001)
Options and asks: Ask for: internal audit plan, if any · link to the corrective actions register (ISO 27001)
Build notes: The control register is the Controls tab of this file unless the client keeps one elsewhere; with a compliance platform, describe the mapping, owners, linked evidence and automated tests there. ISO 27001 statements only when it's in scope; include internal audit also at Enterprise stage (GV-10) or whenever the client runs internal audits. Name the external audits from Framework Scope. Light depth: a section of the Information Security Policy.

Purpose: Makes sure vendor relationships are assessed and managed, to mitigate the risks of outsourcing and using third-party products.
Owners:
Accountable: Governance Lead
Responsible: Technical Lead
Sections and tables: Scope and purpose · Responsibilities: approval and ownership · New vendor assessment criteria · Vendor register (fields) · Annual review
Options and asks:
Options: ESG impacts in the register when the client reports on ESG · commercial checks (business case, alternatives, cost) for larger teams.
Ask for: who approves new vendors · where the vendor register lives
Build notes: Use this one title wherever other policies refer to it. Keep the assessment proportionate for small teams: keep the security, accreditation and dependency checks. Follow the Vendor management shape: Centralised has one approver; Federated or Distributed has each vendor's owner assess against this standard and record it centrally (VM-01). Register fields should match the Vendors tab. For critical vendors and subservice organisations, the annual review covers their assurance reports and the complementary controls the company must operate (VM-02).

Purpose: Sets the company's approach to managing incidents consistently and effectively, with the roles, responsibilities and requirements that apply to every incident.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Operations lead
Sections and tables: Definitions and purpose · Emergency Response Team (table: Title | Contact | Role in response) · How incidents are found · Reporting and logging · Severity (3×3 grid: urgency × impact → S1 to S5) · Target resolution times · Handling aims · Post-incident review (template) · Oversight
Options and asks: Ask for: incident reporting channel · Emergency Response Team members and contact numbers · where incidents are logged
Build notes: The severity grid, targets and definitions are library defaults (Settings to confirm): check they fit and that targets meet customer commitments. Who leads follows the Incident response shape (security-led, coordinated or engineering-led). Use the forums the client already has for oversight (Operating Cadence); don't create meetings. Bugs found before production aren't incidents. The ERT table repeats in the response, recovery and continuity plans: keep it identical, and never invent a phone number. The reporting channel must exist and be monitored (CO-01).

Built from: POL-12.05–12.08 · part of the Incident Management Policy
Purpose: Sets out the processes, steps and pre-defined plans for mitigating and resolving incidents.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Operations lead
Sections and tables: How the plans fit · Major incident scenarios (data breach, system security breach, system outage) · Response steps (preparation, identification and classification, containment, eradication, recovery, closure) · Stakeholder communications · Notification requirements (one line per law) · Testing the plans
Options and asks:
Options: a fourth scenario, a public relations event.
Ask for: Emergency Response Team contacts · who approves external communications
Build notes: Notification rules only for laws that apply, from the Requirement lines below, confirmed by the client's counsel: laws change, so check the current rule first. Customer notice must meet the timeframes in Service Commitments (IR-03). Containment weighs how sensitive the exposed data is, how many users are affected, reputational damage, the cause and whether it could get worse; when in doubt, assess before acting. Light depth: a section of the Incident Response Policy.

Purpose: Sets the roles, responsibilities, software development lifecycle and key requirements for secure and reliable software and systems development.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Engineering lead
Sections and tables: Scope (code; infrastructure as code or approved configuration changes) · Delivery roles · Change requests (ticket, acceptance criteria, impact assessment) · Approval into the backlog · Prioritisation and planning · Development: separate environments, version control and peer review, automated pipeline, testing, release approval, release practices · Emergency changes · Test data
Options and asks:
Options: automated job schedules in scope · Product Owner and Customer Success roles where they exist · planning cadence · user acceptance testing, release checklist, release notes, post-implementation review.
Ask for: who approves releases · planning cadence · backlog prioritisation criteria, if any
Build notes: Describe the path changes really take: tickets and approvers (Traditional approval) or pull requests and pipeline gates (Agile, DevSecOps, Empowered developers); approval into the backlog is a statement only for Traditional approval. If Release Frequency is N/A, scope the policy to configuration changes. Founders may deploy directly (AI Guidance 4.1). With no ticketing tool, say where changes are recorded, such as pull requests. Control CM-07 has emergency changes reviewed and approved within two business days. Confirm the test-data sentence; if production data is used in testing, say so and keep the safeguards.

Purpose: Makes sure the company can respond to major adverse events that threaten critical business functions or services, keeping service to customers, support for employees and critical operations running.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Operations lead
Sections and tables: Events covered · Roles · Business impact analysis (table: Function | RTO | Consequence) · Continuity scenarios (table: Scenario | Main implications | Response; at least loss of key personnel and outage of a critical system or provider) · Communication · Information security continuity · Testing and review (test record template)
Options and asks:
Options: an external security partner retained on call.
Ask for: key business functions and their recovery times · key-person dependencies · Emergency Response Team contacts · company-wide communication channel
Build notes: A plan, not a policy: it needs the client's real functions, people and providers. Propose the BIA starting table (Settings to confirm), then confirm every row. Service RTOs must agree with the Disaster Recovery Plans and Service Commitments. Name the real key people, and the providers from Infrastructure, Hosting Platform and Subservice Providers. Customer notices use the Status Page when the brain has one. Light depth: one Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy.

Purpose: Prepares the company to recover critical systems and data after a major incident, with the roles, practical steps and tests that prove the plan works.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Operations lead
Sections and tables: Roles · Recovery capabilities · Recovery tooling · RTO and RPO · Recovery strategy · Database restore steps (numbered runbook) · Failover steps · Testing and review (test record template)
Options and asks:
Options: recovery capabilities, stating only what is configured (multiple availability zones, automated snapshots, replicated backups, restore steps, recovery steps, support contacts) · failover steps only where failover is configured.
Ask for: RTO and RPO · what recovery is configured (zones, replication, failover) · the restore runbook
Build notes: Recovery steps are client-specific runbooks: write them from the provider's current documentation and have the Technical Lead confirm. RTO and RPO have no default: they must match commitments and be provable by a test, so ask and never assume a value. The capabilities list must be identical to the Backup Policy. Default strategy is backup and restore unless failover exists. Light depth: part of one Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy.

Purpose: Sets responsibilities and requirements for protecting the availability, integrity and confidentiality of data, including the company's recovery objectives and customer or operational requirements.
Owners:
Accountable: Technical Lead
Responsible: Operations lead
Sections and tables: Backup practices · Backup tooling · Production databases and restore tests (table)
Options and asks: Ask for: backup schedule and retention · where backups are stored
Build notes: Short. Control BC-01 expects backups to be encrypted, retained to schedule and stored apart from production: confirm, then state it. List the real databases. Restore test frequency: annually, or quarterly where availability is committed and in scope (AV-01). Light depth: a section of the Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Policy.

Purpose: Sets the practices that stop technical vulnerabilities in the company's network and systems being exploited: identifying, assessing, logging and resolving them.
Owners:
Accountable: Security lead
Responsible: Security lead
Sections and tables: Delivery roles · Identification: code review and scanning, network scanning, penetration testing, further identification · Risk rating (OWASP 3×3 grid) · Vulnerability log (fields) · Resolution timeframes · Management reporting
Options and asks:
Options: secure development training (a control from Scaleup stage, HR-05) · web application scanning when a web app scanner is named · third-party vulnerability assessments.
Ask for: resolution timeframes the team can meet · where vulnerabilities are tracked
Build notes: Auditors test the timeframes, so set ones the team will hit and no slower than customer commitments (statement POL-10.06 and Settings to confirm). Describe only scanning that runs; with no scanner, describe the dependency checks in control TV-02. TV-01 scans at least weekly with a tool, otherwise quarterly. If no penetration test is planned, flag the gap rather than stating one. Where there is both a CISO and a security manager, the CISO is accountable. In the OWASP grid, high impact with low likelihood rates Medium. Light depth: a section of the Operations Security Policy.

Built from: POL-14 · POL-14.01–14.08 · also when a privacy law is in Regulatory Drivers
Purpose: Sets out the company's privacy program (internal, Part 1) and its public privacy notice (website, Part 2).
Owners:
Accountable: Privacy officer
Responsible: Compliance Owner
Sections and tables: Part 1, privacy program: legal review and structure · regulations that apply (table: Privacy regulation | Purpose and regulator) · obligations with references (Privacy obligations below) · Part 2, website notice: introduction and role · how we use personal data · personal data we may collect · when we share personal data · your rights · sub-processors and contacts
Options and asks:
Options: Part 2, only if the client has no published privacy policy or asks for a redraft · the uses, data types, sharing cases and rights that are true for the service.
Ask for: privacy contact details · controller or processor role · personal data collected and why · sub-processors and data locations
Build notes: A draft for legal review, always carrying the disclaimer; never publish a notice without the client's legal sign-off. If a privacy policy is already published, build Part 1 only and keep it consistent with the published notice. Print references only for laws that apply, and drop an obligation none of them reference. Check Customer Geography and Country/Region(s): if a region is served but its law isn't in Regulatory Drivers, ask. The rights list isn't adjusted per law: check each right against the laws that apply. Never invent contact details.

Purpose: Sets the objectives, roles and responsibilities, and requirements for the company's use of AI systems.
Owners:
Accountable: Governance Lead
Responsible: Technical Lead
Sections and tables: AI objectives · AI principles · Key risks (recorded in the risk register) · Interested parties and impacts (table, when AI reliance is Assistive, AI-native or Agentic) · Lifecycle and improvement (AI in the product) · Data management (approved tools and permitted data) · Reporting concerns · Governance practices · AI ethics committee (Formal committees only)
Options and asks:
Options: objectives, principles, risks and governance practices are menus; pick the few that are true for the client · AI resourcing · ethics committee only where formal committees already exist.
Ask for: what AI is used for · potential impacts on users, customers, employees and society · who takes AI concerns
Build notes: Scale it to AI reliance: workplace-only use needs objectives, principles, data rules and reporting; AI in the product adds impacts, lifecycle and monitoring. Control AI-02 expects the approved AI tools and the data staff may enter into them to be named: add them once the client confirms. AI-03: provider terms must stop customer data being used to train models. For Agentic reliance, the policy must also cover production agents per controls AI-06 to AI-19: the agent inventory, accountable owner and risk assessment, agent identities and access, agent-made changes, activity logging and incident authority, and customer-directed changes (statements POL-15.06 to POL-15.11).
